chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym al-Ṣaḥḥāf, from Dharīḥ al-Muḥāribī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام used to say: “Indeed, I dislike for a man to remain well in the world such that nothing from the afflictions befalls him.”

key_terms.أَكْرَهُ: I dislike or regard as undesirable
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the present worldly life as opposed to the hereafter
key_terms.الْمَصَائِبِ: afflictions, trials, or calamities that come upon a person
key_terms.يُصِيبَهُ: to befall him or strike him
key_terms.يُعَافَى: to be kept safe, healthy, or spared from harm in worldly life

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام dislike that a person pass through life without any affliction?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys that being untouched by hardship in the world is not regarded as desirable for a believer. Afflictions are presented as a meaningful part of worldly life, indicating spiritual benefit and moral testing rather than mere misfortune.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Nuaym Al Sahhaf, from Zareeh Al Muharby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not like it for the man that he be healthy in the world but is not hit by anything from the difficulties’.
en.sarwar: 19. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Husayn ibn Nu’aiim al-Sahhaf from Dhurayh al-Muharibi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) has said, ‘I do not like a person’s (total freedom from) suffering in the world from misfortunes.’”
